# Arcus Testnet Volume Bot — agent guide (llms.txt)

> Machine-readable operating manual for this repository. If you are an AI agent
> or a developer picking this up cold, read this file top to bottom before
> changing anything. It describes what the bot does, the venue it trades, the
> exact wire rules that make orders valid, and the invariants you must not break.

Repository: automated market-making / volume bot for the **Arcus** exchange
(perpetuals + Stock Token spot), built and tuned for **testnet**.
Language: Python 3.11+, stdlib-only except `cryptography` and `websockets`.
Entry point: `python -m arcusbot <command>`.

---

## 1. Objective (read this first)

The goal is **not** directional profit. It is:

> generate as much trading volume as possible on testnet, while net PnL after
> exchange fees stays greater than or equal to zero — i.e. the captured spread
> must cover the fees the volume incurs.

Everything in the codebase follows from that single sentence:

| Requirement | How it is enforced | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Volume | Continuous two-sided quoting, both sides re-posted after every fill | `strategy.MarketWorker.tick` |
| Don't lose funds | Position caps, drawdown kill switch, reduce-only closes, collateral floor | `risk.RiskManager` |
| Bounded exposure | Sizing derived from an explicit budget + untouchable reserve | `capital.plan_capital` |
| Cover fees | Every quoted pair must clear `fees(maker+maker) + buffer + volatility` | `strategy.MarketWorker.edge_bps` |
| Measure it | Per-fill average-cost ledger, fee-aware net PnL, `feeCoverageRatio` | `pnl.PnLTracker` |
| Be aggressive safely | ALO (post-only) quotes can never pay taker fees; only inventory closes cross | `strategy`, `sim` |

The single most important number the bot reports is **`netBpsOfVolume`**:
net PnL expressed in basis points of the volume that produced it. Positive means
the volume paid for itself. `feeCoverageRatio > 1` means the same thing.

---

## 2. Quick start

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt

# 1. Prove the machinery offline — no network, no keys, deterministic.
.venv/bin/python -m arcusbot selftest --venue sim

# 2. Find a spread that clears fees (multi-seed, offline).
.venv/bin/python -m arcusbot sweep --sweep-spreads 6,10,20 --sweep-seeds 4

# 3. Point at the real testnet, read-only.
.venv/bin/python -m arcusbot preflight
.venv/bin/python -m arcusbot quote          # what it WOULD place
.venv/bin/python -m arcusbot run --mode dry-run --port 8080

# 4. Go live on testnet (small, time-boxed).
.venv/bin/python -m arcusbot run --mode live --duration 900 --notional 25 --port 8080
```

Credentials come from `.env` (see `.env.example`). Generate them in the web app
at <https://testnet.arcus.xyz/api-keys>, or scripted via `tools/onboard.py`.

---

## 3. Commands

| Command | Network? | Sends orders? | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selftest` | no | to the simulator | End-to-end run + hard assertions on the accounting |
| `sweep` | no | to the simulator | Measure net bps across spreads/seeds |
| `preflight` | read-only | no | Gateway, key registration, markets, fees, balance, sizing |
| `markets` | read-only | no | Tick/step/notional grid per market |
| `quote` | read-only | no | Print the exact intents the strategy would emit now |
| `run --mode dry-run` | read-only | no | Full loop, logs intents instead of signing |
| `run --mode live` | yes | **yes** | Real signed orders |
| `report` | no | no | Reprint the last session's PnL report |
| `history` | no | no | Lifetime totals, today's loss, recent sessions |

Useful flags: `--venue sim|arcus`, `--markets BTC-USD,ETH-USD`, `--notional 25`,
`--spread-bps 10`, `--duration 900`, `--volume-target 5000`, `--port 8080`, `--json`.

---

## 4. The venue: Arcus wire rules that actually matter

Source: <https://docs.arcus.xyz/llms.txt>. These are the rules that cause silent
failures if you get them wrong.

### 4.1 Endpoints
- REST testnet `https://api.testnet.arcus.xyz`, WS `wss://api.testnet.arcus.xyz/v1/ws`
- Mainnet `https://api.arcus.xyz` / `wss://api.arcus.xyz/v1/ws`
  (the bot **refuses** `--mode live` on mainnet by design — `config.validate`)

### 4.2 Authentication
API key = the **public half of an Ed25519 keypair**. Three headers on every
mutating call: `X-API-Key`, `X-Timestamp` (Unix **nanoseconds**, ±30s of server
clock), `X-Signature` (128 lowercase hex).

**Scheme 1 — typed canonical payload** (`placeOrder` op 1, `cancelOrder` op 2,
`modifyOrder` op 3, untriggered TPSL op 4). The signed message *is* the compact
key-sorted JSON payload — no prefix, no concatenation:

```
{"ad":"0x…","ai":N,"c":"…","ct":N,"g":N,"m":N,"op":1,"p":N,"q":N,"r":0,"s":N,"t":N,"v":1}
```

- `ad` master address, **lowercased** — the only case-folded field
- `c` clientId — **omitted entirely when empty**, otherwise signed byte-for-byte
  in the exact case you send it (`id` likewise)
- `ct` == the `X-Timestamp` you send, in nanoseconds
- `g` goodTilTime in **nanoseconds** = body `goodTilTime` (µs) × 1000
- `p` integer ticks = `price / tickSize`; `q` integer quantums = `size / stepSize`
  — the division must be **exact**, and the divisor is always the market's
  top-level `tickSize` even inside a coarser `tickTiers` band
- `r` reduce-only as integer `0`/`1` — never a JSON boolean
- `s` side (0 buy / 1 sell), `t` TIF (0 GTT, 1 FOK, 2 IOC, 3 ALO), `v` = 1

**Scheme 2 — legacy** (`cancelAllOrders`, `setLeverage`,
`scheduleCancelAllDeadMansSwitch`, WS `authenticate`):
`ed25519(str(timestamp_ns) + action + canonical_json(body))`, no delimiters.
`action` is the camelCase final path segment.

**Batches** are Scheme 1 applied per element, all sharing one `X-Timestamp` as
each element's `ct`; every element carries its own `signature`. The envelope
`X-Signature` header must still be **present** (value unverified) — omit it and
every element fails with `invalid order signature`.

### 4.3 Order rules that reject you
- `goodTilTime` is **required on every order including IOC and FOK**, and must
  be **≥ ~1 month in the future**. It is replay protection, not just expiry.
- Body `goodTilTime` is epoch **microseconds** (string); the signed `g` is that
  × 1000.
- Body `price`/`quantity` stay **decimal strings** and must match the values the
  integer `p`/`q` were derived from.
- Minimum order notional **$5** (`quantity × price`); reduce-only is exempt.
- `MARKET` orders must be `timeInForce: IOC` and still carry a `price` — a
  protective bound within **10%** of mark, else
  `MarketPriceSlippageToleranceTooHigh`. Most integrations just send an
  aggressive LIMIT instead; this bot does.
- Single-order TPSL via `POST /v1/placeOrder` returns **501** — TPSL must go
  through `batchPlaceOrders` groupings.
- **There is no cancel-on-disconnect.** Dropping the socket does not cancel
  resting orders. Either cancel explicitly on exit (this bot does) or arm the
  dead man's switch (`RISK_DEAD_MANS_SWITCH_S`).

### 4.4 Async execution
`placeOrder`/`cancelOrder`/batches return **202 ACK** (sometimes 200 with state).
The HTTP body is an acknowledgement, **not** the outcome. Definitive lifecycle
lives on the `orders` and `userFills` WebSocket channels. Treat exchange
`positions` as inventory truth and reconcile against it — this bot does so every
loop (`engine._sync_positions`).

### 4.5 Rate limits (two independent layers)
- **Per IP**: 1,500 weight bucket, refilling 25/s. `markets`/`fills`/`candles`
  cost 20; `bbo`/`account`/`positions` cost 2; `setLeverage` costs 125;
  **order writes cost 0**. `rest.IPBudget` mirrors this client-side and sleeps
  pre-emptively rather than discovering 429s.
- **Per subaccount**: order pool 20,000 / cancel pool 40,000, growing with
  lifetime volume (`+1` unit per $0.10 traded). `cancelAllOrders` charges a flat
  1,000 against the cancel pool. Exhausted → a 1-action-per-10s drip.
- A 429 body's `reason` field says which layer rejected (`ip`, `account_empty`,
  `account_partial`); `retryAfterMs` is exact. Prefer WS subscriptions over REST
  polling — that is the whole reason this bot streams.

### 4.6 Rejection reasons worth handling
`POST_ONLY_WOULD_CROSS` (free — an ALO that would take; just re-quote),
`SELF_TRADE`, `UNDERCOLLATERALIZED`, `IOC_CANCELED`, `FOK_FAILED`,
`REDUCE_ONLY_WOULD_INCREASE`, `DUPLICATE_CLIENT_ID`, `POSITION_SIZE_CAP_EXCEEDED`,
`OPEN_INTEREST_CAP_EXCEEDED`, `FILL_WILL_EXCEED_TRADING_BOUND`.

### 4.7 Fees
Maker/taker in **ppm** from `GET /v1/feetiers` (never hard-code; high tiers can
be negative = maker rebate). Perp fee tiers publish closer to launch. **Spot is
free at launch.** Funding is a transfer between traders, not a fee.

### 4.8 Spot (Stock Tokens) is not an order book
Spot is an RFQ + AMM **router**: request a quote, sign an intent with a
client-side `minBuyAmount` floor, the server settles the single best firm quote
atomically on-chain. There is nothing to rest, so `SpotVolumeStrategy` emits
round-trip *intents* gated on quoted slippage rather than posting orders.

### 4.9 Real-world-asset markets
Equity/commodity perps have `regularTradingHours`. Outside RTH they use a higher
`offHoursInitialMarginFraction` and enforce hard `upperTradingBound` /
`lowerTradingBound` price bands. `MarketState.within_bounds` refuses to quote
outside them; sizing must respect the off-hours margin or you get
`UNDERCOLLATERALIZED`.

---

## 5. Architecture

```
cli.py         argument parsing, logging, command dispatch
config.py      typed config from env/.env + validate()  <- refuses live-on-mainnet
capital.py     budget -> clip/position/loss limits, reserves, mid-run re-sizing
referral.py    referral links + $1B VIP milestone arithmetic
session.py     durable state across restarts: lifetime totals, daily loss,
               drawdown baseline, crash-loop breaker
signing.py     Ed25519, Scheme 1 typed payloads, Scheme 2 legacy
scaling.py     decimal <-> ticks/quantums, tier-aware snapping, slippage clamp
rest.py        signed REST client + client-side IP weight budget
ws.py          reconnecting WebSocket, channel fan-out, signed RPC
book.py        BookState (L2/BBO) + MarketState (mark, bands, realised vol EWMA)
pnl.py         FeeSchedule (ppm), Fill, average-cost MarketPnL, PnLTracker
risk.py        per-order gate + global verdict (OK/THROTTLE/FLATTEN/HALT)
strategy.py    MarketWorker (perp quoting) + SpotVolumeStrategy (RFQ)
sim.py         offline paper exchange: adverse + uninformed flow, real fee math
sweep.py       multi-seed edge measurement
engine.py      the async loop wiring all of the above
dashboard.py   stdlib HTTP live dashboard + /api/status JSON
```

Data flow per loop (`engine._loop_once`):

```
ws frames -> BookState/MarketState -> observe_vol()
          -> PnLTracker.set_marks()
          -> RiskManager.evaluate()  ->  OK | THROTTLE | FLATTEN | HALT
          -> MarketWorker.tick(can_open)  -> [OrderIntent]
          -> risk.check_order() per intent
          -> REST placeOrder / cancelOrder   (0 IP weight)
          -> userFills/orders/positions stream back -> PnLTracker
```

---

## 6. Strategy: `volume-maker`

1. Compute the **required edge**:
   `max(configured_spread, fee_round_trip + buffer, fee_floor + vol_multiplier × realised_vol)`.
   The volatility term is the adverse-selection premium — a static spread in a
   moving market is how makers bleed.
2. Post one ALO bid and one ALO ask around mid, offset by half the edge, skewed
   against current inventory so the reducing side is more attractive.
3. Snap to the tick grid, then **re-verify** the pair still clears the edge
   (coarse ticks can silently erase a 1–2 bps margin).
4. On a fill: the reducing side becomes **reduce-only**, sized to cover the
   position, priced at `entry ± required_edge` so the round trip books positive
   gross edge. Both legs resting = maker/maker = the cheapest possible cycle.
5. Escalate to a reduce-only **IOC** (paying taker fees, crossing the spread)
   only when inventory is oversized, older than `BOT_INVENTORY_MAX_AGE_S`, or on
   shutdown. Carrying unhedged inventory is the bigger, unbounded risk — fees
   are bounded and known.

`ping-pong` = same skeleton, always taker-closes (more volume, worse edge).
`spot-rfq` = zero-fee spot round trips gated on quoted slippage.

---

## 6b. Capital management

Two sizing modes. **fixed** (default) takes the notionals literally from config.
**capital** activates when `BOT_CAPITAL_USD` or `BOT_CAPITAL_PCT` is non-zero
and derives everything from a budget:

```
deployable      = min(budget, equity − reserve)
exposure_budget = deployable × leverage × utilisation
per_market      = exposure_budget ÷ market_count
clip            = per_market ÷ BOT_CAPITAL_CLIPS
max_position    = per_market
max_inventory   = per_market × BOT_CAPITAL_INVENTORY_FRACTION
```

Rules an agent must not break when touching `capital.py`:

- **`utilisation` < 1 is deliberate.** It is the gap between what margin allows
  and what the bot deploys. Setting it to 1 invites liquidation.
- **The reserve is enforced twice** — subtracted from the budget *and* used as
  `min_free_collateral_usd`. Only the second makes it real.
- **Both `_USD` and `_PCT` set → the lower wins.**
- **Unknown equity never guesses.** Mode becomes `unfunded` and the fixed
  notionals stand.
- **A clip under $5 is raised to $5**; a budget that cannot fund even one clip
  halts at startup with an actionable message rather than failing every order.
- **Capital sizing feeds the risk manager, never bypasses it.**
- Re-sizing happens only past `BOT_CAPITAL_RESIZE_PCT` equity drift, so caps do
  not jitter under open inventory.

Full detail: `docs/CAPITAL.md`. Tests: `tests/test_capital.py`.

## 6c. Referral and the $1B VIP milestone

`referral.py` holds signup links (`ARCUS_REFERRAL_TESTNET` default `AAAA` →
`https://testnet.arcus.xyz/ref/AAAA`; `ARCUS_REFERRAL_MAINNET` default
`AIAGENT` → `https://app.arcus.xyz/ref/AIAGENT`). **Referral attribution is a
signup-time browser concern — never inject a code into an order payload.** The
banner is suppressed by `BOT_SHOW_REFERRAL=false`.

`vip_progress()` tracks the advertised "$1B volume unlocks VIP" target and
reports percent complete, ETA at the current rate, and — the number that
actually matters — `projectedPnlAtTargetUsd = remaining × netBps / 10_000`.
At a negative edge that is a large negative number, which is the honest signal
that chasing the milestone costs money. Do not present VIP progress without it.

## 6d. State across restarts

`session.py` persists what a process lifetime would otherwise forget:
lifetime volume/fees/PnL, the UTC-day loss, the drawdown high-water mark and a
count of consecutive unclean exits. Written atomically to
`state/session.json` on shutdown, reloaded on boot.

Why it matters: **a bot that forgets its losses on restart has no risk limits.**
Halt on a $25 drawdown, get restarted by a supervisor, lose $25 again — every
session reports itself healthy while the account bleeds.

Rules:

- **Daily loss carries.** `RiskManager.effective_daily_loss()` = this session's
  loss + what was already booked today. Past the limit the bot refuses to start.
- **Drawdown is measured from the all-time peak** when `RISK_CARRY_DRAWDOWN` is
  on (default) — drawdown is a property of the account, not a process.
- **Open positions are NOT persisted.** The exchange is the authority on
  inventory; a stored belief that contradicts the venue is worse than no belief.
- **Corruption is survivable** — quarantine to `session.corrupt`, start fresh,
  warn. Never refuse to run because of a bad state file.
- **Diagnostics must not mutate it.** `selftest` and `sweep` force
  `persist_state=false`.
- Clean exits (runtime limit, volume target, signal, cancellation) reset the
  crash counter; anything else increments it.

## 7. Risk model

Per order (`risk.check_order`): market ONLINE, min notional, max order size,
inside off-hours bands, price not stale, open-order cap, order-rate cap,
projected position under notional cap, free collateral above floor.
**Reduce-only orders bypass the opening restrictions and are still permitted
after a halt** — the bot must always be able to close what it opened.

Global verdict (`risk.evaluate`):

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `OK` | quote normally |
| `THROTTLE` | cool-down after a 429 / rejection storm |
| `FLATTEN` | stop opening, keep closing (collateral floor, inventory cap, 70% of drawdown limit) |
| `HALT` | kill switch: cancel all, flatten, write report, exit |

Kill switch fires on: max drawdown, max daily loss, N consecutive errors,
runtime limit, volume target reached, auth failure (401/403).

Shutdown is always `cancel-all -> flatten (reduce-only IOC, retried) -> report`.

---

## 8. Invariants — do not break these

1. **Never quote a pair tighter than the fee-derived edge.** Test:
   `test_quoted_spread_always_clears_the_fee_floor`.
2. **Never round a price/size into existence.** `to_ticks`/`to_quantums` raise on
   a non-exact division; sizes always round **down**.
3. **The signed payload and the request body must agree.** Both are built from
   the same snapped decimals in `rest.build_order`.
4. **Reduce-only orders are always allowed**, including post-halt.
5. **Exchange positions are truth**; the local book is reconciled, not trusted.
6. **Fills are idempotent by `tradeId`** — snapshot and stream overlap.
7. **`net = realized + unrealized + funding + rebates − fees`** — asserted in
   `selftest` and `test_net_pnl_identity_includes_fees_and_rebates`.
8. **Live mode on mainnet is refused** in `config.validate()`.
9. **The reserve is never traded into** — it is both subtracted from the budget
   and enforced as the free-collateral floor.
10. **Referral codes never enter an order payload.** Signup-time only.
11. **`.env` is gitignored and never committed**; `.env.example` carries the
    same keys with no secrets.
12. **Risk state survives restarts.** Daily loss and drawdown carry over; a
    restart must never hand back a spent loss budget.
13. **The required edge never falls below `BOT_MIN_EDGE_BPS`**, even at rebate
    tiers where the fee term goes negative. Quoting both sides at mid would
    maximise adverse selection.

Run `python -m pytest tests -q` (172 tests, no network) after any change.

---

## 9. Configuration

Full list in `.env.example`. The ones that change behaviour most:

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BOT_MODE` | `dry-run` | `live` actually signs and sends |
| `ARCUS_VENUE` | `arcus` | `sim` = offline paper exchange |
| `BOT_MARKETS` | `BTC-USD,ETH-USD` | markets to quote |
| `BOT_ORDER_NOTIONAL_USD` | `25` | per-clip size (min $5 engine floor) |
| `BOT_CAPITAL_USD` / `_PCT` | `0` | budget to deploy; enables derived sizing |
| `BOT_RESERVE_USD` | `0` | equity never touched; also the collateral floor |
| `BOT_CAPITAL_UTILISATION` | `0.5` | share of available leverage deployed |
| `BOT_SPREAD_BPS` | `10` | target round-trip edge |
| `BOT_FEE_BUFFER_BPS` | `1` | margin required over fees |
| `BOT_VOL_EDGE_MULTIPLIER` | `1.5` | spread widening per bps of realised vol |
| `BOT_INVENTORY_SKEW_BPS` | `8` | max quote shift at full inventory |
| `BOT_MAX_POSITION_NOTIONAL_USD` | `150` | hard per-market position cap |
| `BOT_INVENTORY_MAX_AGE_S` | `90` | when to cross the spread to flatten |
| `RISK_MAX_DRAWDOWN_USD` | `25` | kill switch |
| `RISK_MIN_FREE_COLLATERAL_USD` | `50` | flatten-only floor |
| `BOT_VOLUME_TARGET_USD` | `0` | stop after this much volume (0 = unlimited) |
| `BOT_METRICS_PORT` | `0` | dashboard port (0 = off) |
| `BOT_MIN_EDGE_BPS` | `1` | absolute spread floor; survives rebate tiers |
| `BOT_PERSIST_STATE` | `true` | carry risk state across restarts |
| `RISK_CARRY_DRAWDOWN` | `true` | drawdown measured from the all-time peak |
| `RISK_MAX_RESTART_CRASHES` | `0` | `>0` refuses to start after N unclean exits |

---

## 10. Monitoring

`--port 8080` serves a live dashboard plus:
- `GET /api/status` — full engine status (the same JSON written to `state/status.json`)
- `GET /api/report` — PnL block only
- `GET /healthz`

Artifacts: `state/status.json` (live), `state/fills.jsonl` (append-only journal),
`state/report-<session>.json` + `report-latest.json`, `logs/bot-YYYYMMDD.log`.

Health checklist while running: `netBpsOfVolume` ≥ 0, `feeCoverageRatio` ≥ 1,
`makerShare` high (taker legs are the expensive ones), `risk.state` = OK,
`ws.connected` true, `rejects` not climbing (a few `POST_ONLY_WOULD_CROSS` is
normal and free), `ipBudget.tokens` not pinned at 0.

---

## 11. Known limits / honest caveats

- The simulator is a **machinery test, not a market model**. It proves the bot
  quotes, fills, closes, accounts and halts correctly. Whether a given spread is
  profitable is a property of the *real* venue's flow — measure it on testnet.
- Under mostly-adverse flow (`SIM_UNINFORMED_RATE` at its 0.25 default) the
  strategy loses ~1.5-2.6 bps; with balanced two-sided flow (0.35+) it clears
  fees, ~+0.5 to +1.0 bps at a 10 bps spread. That is the correct and expected
  behaviour of a market maker, not a bug to tune away.
- Testnet contract addresses in `config.py` **change on every redeploy**. Verify
  before using `tools/fund_testnet.py`.
- Perp fee tiers are not final; the bot reads them live and falls back to a
  conservative 2/5 bps if the endpoint is unavailable.
- Spot RFQ execution emits intents; wiring the settlement transaction requires
  the RFQ endpoints and a wallet signer, which are deliberately not automated.
